quote: On the main page of the repository, to the right of the list of files, click **Activity**.
To filter by activity type, select the **All activity** dropdown menu, then click an activity type.
Above the file content, click **Blame**.
To return to the raw code view, above the file content, click **Code**.
If you are viewing a Markdown file, above the file content, you can also click **Preview** to return to the view with Markdown formatting applied.
In the upper-right corner of the file view, click **Raw**.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Code frequency**.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Commits**.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Contributors**.
Optionally, to view contributors during a specific time period, to the right of "Contributors," click **Period: All**.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Dependency graph**.
Optionally, to view the repositories and packages that depend on your repository, under "Dependency graph", click **Dependents**.
Under your repository name, click **Issues** or **Pull requests**.
Above the list of issues or pull requests, click **Labels**.
In the list of labels, click a label.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Forks**.
Optionally, to sort the list by most starred forks, most recently updated forks, most open issues, or most open pull requests, click **Sort**, then choose an option from the dropdown menu.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
In the left sidebar, click **Network**.
Under your repository name, click **Insights**.
Optionally, to choose a different time period, select the **Period** dropdown menu in the upper-right corner of the Pulse overview.
From the file tree view on the left, select the branch dropdown menu, then click **View all branches**.

**Active branches:** The **Active** view shows all branches (excluding the default branch) that anyone has committed to within the last three months, ordered by the branches with the most recent commits first.
**All branches:** The **All** view shows the default branch, followed by all other branches ordered by the branches with the most recent commits first.
To the right of the list of files, click **Releases**.
At the top of the Releases page, click **Releases**.
To the right of the list of files, click **Releases**.
At the top of the page, click **Tags**.
Under your repository name, click **Actions**.
Click the menu icon and, in the sidebar, click **Dashboards**.
Click the menu icon and, in the sidebar, click **Explore**.
Locate the **Print/export** section in the left panel of the page.
Select **Download as PDF** from the list.
To do this, click **Create a book** under **Print/export** on the left sidebar in Wikipedia.
This will open the Book creator page; click **Start book creator** to get started.
To do this, click the **Print/export** link on the left sidebar in Wikipedia when you're on an article you want to save.
Click **Download as PDF** to have Wikipedia automatically generate a PDF copy of this article.
Alternatively, you can open any Wikipedia page and choose **Book Creator** from the toolbox menu in the right sidebar.
Next browse to any Wikipedia page and click the “**Add this page to your book**” link to include that article into your ebook.
On the left hand side of the screen, you should see a link that says “**Print/Export**”.
Click this, and you’ll see some options – you’ll want to click on “**Download as PDF**”.
Look for "**Tools**" on the left side of the page and click on "**Cite this page**."
Use the **export** button in the top bar to open the export sidebar to get OpenStreetMap XML data for an area.
Click on the **Filter** button, open **Location** and select **Country**.
In the top navigation bar, under the Page name, select the **Tools** drop-down menu.
In the **Print/export** section select **Download as PDF**.
You can view a page's history by clicking the "**View history**" tab at the top of the associated page (pictured).
To compare a revision with its predecessor, click "**prev**".

A link to "**Page information**" is in the **Tools** panel on the desktop site, which is typically available from the three dots menu at the top right of an article (it can be a sidebar if you're enabled that option).
A permalink can be made by clicking '**Permanent link**' in the sidebar's toolbox or by accessing a prior revision of a page from its page history tab.
Within the **Tools** section at the top-right of every page (in the standard view) is a link labeled "**What links here**".
